effect_mechanism: A buffer keeps, or puts back, a strip of woody vegetation between the field or the cut-block and the channel, and biodiversity responds through the habitat held in that strip and through the water it filters. Width governs the habitat side: streams with buffers of 30 m or more showed no impact of harvest on invertebrates, while narrower strips changed species diversity in proportion to their width [ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_1]; bird assemblages needed more, with 150 and 175 m argued as the widths that would maintain 90 and 95% of preharvest species, and more than 50 m to hold bird densities and prevent changes to community structure [ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_3, ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_4]; moose densities were greater in 60 m strips left after harvesting than in blocks that retained no buffer [ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_7]; and trout populations recovered once revegetation by shrubs and trees brought down the stream temperature that had followed harvesting to the margin [ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_2]. The water side works through what the strip stops: buffers reduce sediments and contaminants entering the watercourse, improving the ecological status of waterbodies and favouring pollution-sensitive mayflies, stoneflies and caddisflies over pollutant-tolerant chironomids [ev_biodiversity_outcome_cole20_4]. The Brazilian evidence measures the same relationship from the losing end, and it is the sharpest statement of how little vegetation can be given up: aquatic invertebrate bioindicators declined abruptly after a mean loss of 6.5% of the riparian vegetation within 50 m of the stream, and only 2.9% in the Amazon biome [ev_biodiversity_outcome_dalacorte20_4, ev_biodiversity_outcome_dalacorte20_5], with thresholds lowest in the narrowest buffers, so vegetation close to the water is what carries the effect [ev_biodiversity_outcome_dalacorte20_6]. At landscape scale the buffer is also a corridor: conserving and restoring riparian buffers is credited with enhancing connectivity in fragmented landscapes and letting native species persist in habitat remnants [ev_biodiversity_outcome_meli19_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_meli19_2], and on the Ayuquila the longitudinal continuity of the riverbanks increased and physical habitat quality improved after restoration [ev_biodiversity_outcome_meli19_6]. A model of riparian forest along a river in Belgium finds that the best options raise an index of pollution-sensitive stream insects by up to 96.0%, while the diversity of diatoms (tiny algae) changes little, by up to 5.2% [ev_biodiversity_outcome_witing22_2, ev_biodiversity_outcome_witing22_3].
conditionality: The direction is consistent but, apart from one model, nothing here measures how much biodiversity is gained: the quantities reported are buffer widths and thresholds of vegetation loss, not effect sizes, so the row states a direction rather than a size. Two findings are measured harm rather than a missing gain: overtaxing the nutrient-removal capacity of riparian zones and floodplain wetlands may lead to losses of biodiversity and production of nitrous oxides [ev_biodiversity_outcome_maye07_4], and in urban North Carolina stream restorations the increased temperature and light that stimulate early nutrient uptake had severe consequences for instream biota and shifted the stream toward autotrophy and algal biomass — in projects that bundle channel engineering with riparian replanting and state no share for either [ev_biodiversity_outcome_mcmi14_1]. Much of the width evidence comes from strips left standing after harvesting in forestry [ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_7]: it shows what retaining riparian vegetation does at harvest, not what establishing a strip on cleared farmland would deliver, and the revegetation finding for trout is the closest this row comes to the latter [ev_biodiversity_outcome_lee04_2]. effect_mechanism: The evidence points to a small gain in carbon. The carbon is in the woody biomass the buffer grows, above and below ground: a UK review puts the storage capacity of wooded buffers at an estimated 80 t per hectare per year across both pools [ev_carbon_sequestration_cole20_1]. Measured in planted hybrid poplar buffers on southern Quebec farm streams, carbon in total aboveground biomass reached 52 t per hectare at the most fertile site and as little as 6.4 t per hectare at the least [ev_carbon_sequestration_fort10_1], and aboveground biomass and carbon in the poplars were statistically higher than in the poplar understorey and in the adjacent unmanaged herbaceous buffer [ev_carbon_sequestration_fort10_2] — planting trees, not simply fencing the strip, is what moved the stock. Scaled by model, bringing riparian forest up to the minimum that Costa Rican Forest Law 7575 requires raises the national carbon stock by 1.4%, or 7.0 Mt [ev_carbon_sequestration_lang22_1]. A European model of buffer strips planted on cropland finds the gain in soil carbon substantial in absolute terms, but unlikely to make up much of the soil carbon already lost across Europe [ev_soil_organic_carbon_englund21_7].

The Quebec measurement spreads from 52 down to 6.4 t per hectare between sites of the same planting [ev_carbon_sequestration_fort10_1], so site fertility, not the practice, dominates the outcome; it is also aboveground stock in a young stand, with no soil carbon measured. The Costa Rican 1.4% is a modelled scenario output rather than a measurement, from a study whose authors flag their sediment model as over-estimating erosion on steep ground and their nutrient model as very sensitive to its retention parameter [ev_carbon_sequestration_lang22_1]. The European soil-carbon finding is a model and gives no figure [ev_soil_organic_carbon_englund21_7]. Nothing in this row is measured in a low- or lower-middle-income landscape: Canada, the UK, Costa Rica and the European study area are all classified high-income, and the evidence is temperate apart from the Costa Rican model.

effect_mechanism: This is retention evidence: strips of the existing mature spruce riparian forest left standing between a clear-cut and the stream in boreal Finland, measured against unlogged control streamsides. Width and thinning decided whether the strip held its microclimate. 15-meter strips with or without selective logging, and 30-meter strips with selective logging, were insufficient in maintaining temperature, relative humidity and canopy openness at control levels [ev_microclimate_buffering_olde19_1]; 30-meter strips without selective logging differed only little from controls, although they had significantly lower mean air humidity [ev_microclimate_buffering_olde19_2, ev_microclimate_buffering_olde19_3]; and at 10 m from the stream every buffer except the unlogged 30-meter ones had significantly higher canopy openness than controls [ev_microclimate_buffering_olde19_4].
conditionality: What the evidence shows is that keeping a wide, unthinned strip of mature forest beside a clear-cut holds the streamside microclimate closer to unlogged forest than a narrow or thinned strip does; the direction comes from the failures of the narrow and thinned strips, read the other way round. effect_mechanism: The rating is a small reduction in erosion risk. Most of the large percentages below measure runoff and soil caught in the strip at the stream edge; the one estimate of soil loss avoided on the cropland itself is small. The buffer intercepts overland flow before it reaches the channel: dense switchgrass stops concentrated flow from the field and allows infiltration rates well above the field rate [ev_runoff_reduction_schultz95_1], which cut runoff by 58.3% behind a 7 m switchgrass buffer and 81.5% behind the wider switchgrass-woody buffer over 19 natural events [ev_runoff_reduction_lee03_5, ev_runoff_reduction_lee03_6], and by more than 77% in Kansas grass-shrub plots [ev_runoff_reduction_mank07_2]. What the water no longer carries is trapped: 70% of incoming sediment behind the grass buffer and more than 92% behind the grass-woody buffer under simulated rainfall [ev_sediment_retention_lee00_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee00_2], 95% and 97% over natural events [ev_sediment_retention_lee03_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee03_3] with trapping never falling below 71% in any storm [ev_sediment_retention_lee03_7], 99.7% of suspended-solids mass in pumped-runoff plots [ev_sediment_retention_mank07_1], 97% behind an 8 m grass strip and 91% within the first 4 m [ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_1, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_4, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_2, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_3], and 92% for woody, 72% for grass and 50% for shrub strips in the Guishui catchment against a bare control that trapped 22% [ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_1, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_2, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_3]. Trapping efficiency rises sharply over the first 10 m and then tails off [ev_sediment_retention_cole20_1], and narrow strips are already effective [ev_sediment_retention_osbo93_15, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_3, ev_sediment_retention_schultz95_1, ev_sediment_retention_zhao13_1, ev_sediment_retention_clau00_1]; in Brazilian third-order watersheds, suspended and organic solids fall as riparian forest cover rises [ev_sediment_retention_mello18_1, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_2], and a national model adds 3.9% to sediment retention [ev_sediment_retention_lang22_1]. A US riparian zone that had been cleared and cropped for a long time and was then restored to grass cut sediment concentration in overland flow by 92% [ev_sediment_retention_dosskey10_5], and McKergow et al. (2003) found that vegetation restoration of denuded, livestock-trampled riparian zones reduced catchment sediment export from over 100 to less than 10 kilograms per hectare per year within one year, mainly by reducing bank erosion and stabilising the stream channel [ev_sediment_retention_dosskey10_6]. The second pathway is the bank itself: planting trees stabilises river banks, reducing erosion and sediment loss [ev_streambank_erosion_cole20_1, ev_streambank_erosion_osbo93_17], willow posts held further collapse to an additional 0.3 m of bank through the 1993 floods and streambank integrity was maintained on the planted reach [ev_streambank_erosion_schultz95_1, ev_streambank_erosion_schultz95_2], farmers on the Ayuquila identify tree roots as what avoids riverbank erosion during floods [ev_streambank_erosion_meli19_5], and replacing riparian forest with other land cover brings bank erosion [ev_streambank_erosion_mello18_11]. A European model of strips of willow, poplar or grass planted along watercourses finds they avoid 6.3% of the soil lost to water erosion on cropland in the landscapes where they are set up (1.2% across the EU and UK), and separately catch 19% of all soil lost by water erosion on European cropland [ev_erosion_hazard_englund21_5, ev_sediment_retention_englund21_6].
conditionality: What the buffer traps depends on what the soil is made of: the same plots retained 93% of sand and silt but only 52% of clay [ev_sediment_retention_lee00_3], and a 4 m grass buffer on a 2% slope was almost 100% effective on sandy loams but only 35% effective on silty clay loams [ev_sediment_retention_cole20_2]. Width buys less than it appears to: retention rises sharply over the first 10 m and then tails off [ev_sediment_retention_cole20_1], widening from 50 m to 100 m added only 4.6% and 4.0% in the two models tested [ev_sediment_retention_sira20_2], and 30 m buffers were unable to prevent increases in stream sedimentation after partial clearcutting [ev_sediment_retention_lee04_2]. Most of the large percentages come from plot-scale experiments under simulated rainfall or pumped runoff rather than field-scale monitoring [ev_sediment_retention_mank07_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee00_1, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_1], and the mass reductions are achieved partly because water infiltrates and is lost, which is not the same as a cleaner stream [ev_runoff_reduction_mank07_2]. Two of the strongest-looking numbers are modelled rather than measured — the 30.5 and 36.2% retention gains from widening Prince Edward Island buffers [ev_sediment_retention_sira20_1] and the Costa Rican 3.9% [ev_sediment_retention_lang22_1] — and the Brazilian values are correlations across a handful of watersheds, not experiments [ev_sediment_retention_mello18_1, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_2]. Two of the bank findings are farmer perception and cited background rather than measurement [ev_streambank_erosion_meli19_5, ev_streambank_erosion_mello18_11]. The two Dosskey-reviewed findings above are themselves citations of other studies, not new measurement by Dosskey et al. [ev_sediment_retention_dosskey10_5, ev_sediment_retention_dosskey10_6]. The measured core is narrow in origin: repeated studies on one Iowa stream, Bear Creek, supply a large share of the runoff and sediment figures [ev_runoff_reduction_lee03_5, ev_sediment_retention_lee00_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee03_1, ev_runoff_reduction_schultz95_1], alongside Kansas, Missouri and Connecticut plots; apart from China and Brazil the whole pool is temperate high-income, and no measurement comes from a low-income farming system. The European figures are model results from rich countries [ev_erosion_hazard_englund21_5, ev_sediment_retention_englund21_6].

effect_mechanism: In the upper-middle-income evidence the effect is trapping in the vegetated strip and holding of the bank. Along the Guishui River, buffer strips reduced average outflow sediment by 92% where the vegetation was woody, 72% where it was grasses and 50% where it was shrubs, against a bare control whose own trapping efficiency was 22% [ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_1, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_2, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_3] — vegetation type, not merely the presence of a strip, sets the size of the effect. In Brazilian third-order watersheds, suspended and organic solids in the stream fall as riparian-zone forest cover rises [ev_sediment_retention_mello18_1, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_2], consistent with buffers of proper design trapping sediment from the runoff passing through [ev_sediment_retention_zhao13_1]. On the bank, replacing riparian forest with other land cover leads to bank erosion [ev_streambank_erosion_mello18_11], and farmers on the Ayuquila identify the role of tree roots in avoiding riverbank erosion during flood events [ev_streambank_erosion_meli19_5].
conditionality: Only the Chinese result is a measured contrast, and it shows how far the effect can fall: a shrub strip trapped 50% where woody vegetation trapped 92%, and the bare control already trapped 22% on its own, so the attributable gain is smaller than the headline [ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_1, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_2, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_3]; those strips were also long-established rather than newly planted. The rest of the row is cited background or an uncited introductory assertion [ev_sediment_retention_zhao13_1, ev_streambank_erosion_mello18_11] and a farmer perception recorded in a case study [ev_streambank_erosion_meli19_5]. effect_mechanism: For rainfed cropping the rating is the same as overall, a small reduction in erosion risk; eight papers name this farming system. Most of the large percentages below measure runoff and soil caught in the strip; the one estimate of soil loss avoided on the cropland itself is small. Below a rainfed row crop the buffer first takes the water out of the flow: switchgrass stops concentrated flow from the field and infiltration runs well above the field rate [ev_runoff_reduction_schultz95_1], cutting runoff by 58.3% behind the 7 m grass buffer and 81.5% behind the wider grass-woody buffer over 19 natural precipitation events [ev_runoff_reduction_lee03_5, ev_runoff_reduction_lee03_6] and by more than 77% in the Kansas plots [ev_runoff_reduction_mank07_2]. Widening the Prince Edward Island buffers from the present 15 m to 100 m is modelled to retain a further 30.5 to 36.2% of the stream sediment load [ev_sediment_retention_sira20_1]. Roots hold the bank itself: forested buffer strips stabilise banks more effectively than grass [ev_streambank_erosion_osbo93_17], willow posts limited further loss to an additional 0.3 m of bank through the 1993 floods, and streambank integrity was maintained on the planted reach [ev_streambank_erosion_schultz95_1, ev_streambank_erosion_schultz95_2]. A European model of strips of willow, poplar or grass planted along watercourses finds they avoid 6.3% of the soil lost to water erosion on cropland in the landscapes where they are set up (1.2% across the EU and UK), and separately catch 19% of all soil lost by water erosion on European cropland [ev_erosion_hazard_englund21_5, ev_sediment_retention_englund21_6].

effect_mechanism: Where riparian vegetation is established or allowed to persist, sediment is intercepted before the channel and the bank is held. Trapping efficiency increases sharply over the first 10 m of buffer and then tails off [ev_sediment_retention_cole20_1], and fairly narrow strips of riparian vegetation reduce sediment input to surface water across the field studies reviewed [ev_sediment_retention_osbo93_15, ev_sediment_retention_schultz95_1, ev_sediment_retention_zhao13_1]. Measured along the Guishui River, outflow sediment fell by 92% under woody vegetation, 72% under grasses and 50% under shrubs, against a bare control trapping 22% [ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_1, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_2, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_3]. In Brazilian watersheds, suspended and organic solids decline as riparian forest cover rises [ev_sediment_retention_mello18_1, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_2], while bringing Costa Rican riparian forest to its legal minimum is modelled to raise sediment retention by 3.9% [ev_sediment_retention_lang22_1]. McKergow et al. Most of the large percentages below measure runoff and soil caught in the strip at the stream edge; the one estimate of soil loss avoided on the cropland itself is small. Switchgrass planted below the cropland stops concentrated flow and lets infiltration run above the field rate [ev_runoff_reduction_schultz95_1], cutting runoff by 58.3% and 81.5% for the grass and the grass-woody buffer [ev_runoff_reduction_lee03_5, ev_runoff_reduction_lee03_6] and by more than 77% in the Kansas plots [ev_runoff_reduction_mank07_2]. effect_mechanism: Three pathways carry this effect. Sediment-bound load settles out in the strip: 70% and more than 92% of incoming sediment trapped under simulated rainfall [ev_sediment_retention_lee00_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee00_2], 95% and 97% over natural events [ev_sediment_retention_lee03_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee03_3], 99.7% of suspended-solids mass in pumped-runoff plots [ev_sediment_retention_mank07_1], and 92% of overland-flow suspended solids after a cropped riparian strip was seeded to fescue [ev_sediment_retention_clau00_1]; at catchment scale, McKergow et al. (2003) found that restoring vegetation to denuded, livestock-trampled riparian zones reduced sediment export from over 100 to less than 10 kilograms per hectare per year within one year, mainly through less bank erosion and a stabilised channel [ev_sediment_retention_dosskey10_6]. Dissolved load is removed as water passes through and is taken up, mainly by plant uptake and by denitrification [ev_nutrient_removal_dosskey10_1]: across 88 buffers in a pooled analysis, mean nitrogen removal effectiveness was 67.5%, at a rate of 0.394 mg per litre per metre of buffer [ev_nutrient_removal_maye07_1, ev_nutrient_removal_maye07_2]; the Bear Creek buffers removed 80% and 94% of total nitrogen over 19 natural events [ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_2, ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_4] and 64 to 72%, rising to 80 to 93% for the wider buffer, under a 25 mm per hour simulation [ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_4, ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_5]; vadose-zone nitrate never exceeded 2 mg per litre inside the Iowa buffer while the adjacent field exceeded 12 [ev_nutrient_removal_schultz95_1, ev_nutrient_removal_schultz95_2]; shallow groundwater nitrate fell by up to 90% behind Illinois buffers [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_1], with reviewed ranges of 79-98% in surface runoff and 68-100% in groundwater for forested strips against 54-84% and 10-60% for grass [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_10, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_11, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_7, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_8, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_9], and phosphorus reductions of 50-85% and 61-83% [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_12, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_13, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_5]; restoring a cropped strip cut overland-flow total Kjeldahl nitrogen 70%, nitrate 83% and total phosphorus 73% [ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_1, ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_2, ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_5]; a separately reviewed US riparian zone that had been cleared and cropped for a long time and was then restored to grass showed a 35% reduction in groundwater nitrate [ev_nutrient_removal_dosskey10_3]; in a long-term study of a trampled, overgrazed pasture riparian zone fenced off from livestock, rapid herbaceous and then woody regrowth was followed by declining stream nutrient levels over the first twelve years [ev_nutrient_removal_dosskey10_7]; along the Guishui River an 18 m woody strip removed 89.8% of total nitrogen and 92.8% of total phosphorus, against 72.3% and 43.9% for grass and shrub strips and 17.62% with no buffer [ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_4, ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_5, ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_6, ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_7, ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_8]; and nutrients accumulate in standing biomass, 770 and 90 kg of nitrogen per hectare in Quebec poplar buffers [ev_nutrient_removal_fort10_1, ev_nutrient_removal_fort10_2, ev_nutrient_removal_blanco04_1, ev_nutrient_removal_blanco04_2, ev_nutrient_removal_blanco04_3, ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_8, ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_9, ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_1]. Third, shade: wooded strips moderate diel fluctuations in stream temperature [ev_stream_temperature_cole20_1], buffers significantly reduced post-harvest temperature increases [ev_stream_temperature_lee04_1, ev_stream_temperature_lee04_2, ev_stream_temperature_lee04_3]. Correlational and modelled work points the same way [ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_3, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_4, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_5, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_6, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_7, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_8, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_9, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_12, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_1, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_2, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_5, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_1, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_2, ev_sediment_retention_zhao13_1, ev_sediment_retention_cole20_1, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_1, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_2, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_3, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_1, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_2, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_3, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_4, ev_sediment_retention_lee00_3, ev_sediment_retention_lee03_7, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_2, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_3, ev_sediment_retention_osbo93_15, ev_sediment_retention_schultz95_1, ev_sediment_retention_sira20_1, ev_nutrient_removal_lang22_1]. Newer sources point the same way. A European model of strips of willow, poplar or grass planted along watercourses finds they would avoid about 33% of all nitrogen reaching water in the EU and UK, and catch 19% of all soil lost by water erosion on cropland [ev_nutrient_removal_englund21_4, ev_sediment_retention_englund21_6]. A Quebec cost study, citing earlier Quebec research second-hand, reports nitrate falling by 47 to 100% and soluble phosphorus by 22 to 89% after wooded strips were planted, and states that without streamside vegetation stream water can be 2 to 10°C warmer [ev_nutrient_removal_simard09_5, ev_stream_temperature_simard09_7].
conditionality: This practice reverses under conditions that are not rare, and the reversal is not confined to frozen or saturated extremes: riparian vegetation improves water quality through nitrogen uptake and denitrification, but in wet, oxygen-poor riparian soils, decomposing plant detritus can set up reducing conditions that desorb phosphate from iron complexes and pass dissolved phosphorus into the stream — the same vegetation-mediated processes working against the practice [ev_nutrient_removal_dosskey10_2]. During most snowmelt runoff events the Guishui strips had little or no effect on nitrogen concentrations and runoff losses of total nitrogen, nitrate and ammonium increased at the buffer outlet — frozen ground turns the sink into a source [ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_9]. During the dormant season both grass and forested Illinois strips released dissolved and total phosphorus to the groundwater [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_2]. Narrow buffers under 15 m actually contributed nitrogen to the riparian zone in six of the pooled studies [ev_nutrient_removal_maye07_3], buffer outflow in the early stages of a natural runoff event can contribute pollutants to surface waters [ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_5], and nutrient-saturated strips act as a source rather than a sink, with the highest risk during high flow, ice thaw and bank erosion [ev_nutrient_removal_cole20_6]. In the Connecticut restoration, total Kjeldahl nitrogen and total phosphorus concentrations increased significantly as groundwater flowed through the restored buffer, and groundwater nitrogen species were otherwise unaffected [ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_3, ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_4]; part of the groundwater nitrate decline there was due to the cessation of fertilisation on the strip, not to the buffer [ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_2]. Mass is not concentration: the Kansas buffers cut total phosphorus and total nitrogen mass by 91.8 and 92.1% but their concentrations by only 42.9 and 44.4% [ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_1], dissolved phosphorus concentration fell by just 16% [ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_3] and nitrate by 10-19% against 48-72% for ammonium [ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_4]. Storm intensity strips the effect away: removal fell to 50 and 28% for the grass buffer and 35% for phosphate behind the wider buffer at 69 mm per hour [ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_6, ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_7], phosphate mass was not significantly reduced at the higher intensity [ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_8], and soluble removal held above 60% in every storm except the most intense [ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_8]. The width evidence contradicts itself — a meta-analysis found no impact of width on nitrogen removal efficiency and increasing width from 4 to 8 m did not reduce soluble herbicide loadings [ev_nutrient_removal_cole20_3, ev_nutrient_removal_cole20_1], while other work says wider is better with diminishing returns and that more than 200 m was needed for ideal efficiency in some cases [ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_3, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_4]. Time matters in both directions: nitrate reductions in the early stages of restoration may be much less than the figures reported for established buffers, which should not be extrapolated [ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_5]; and in one restored stream woody vegetation only established 13-17 years on, then shaded out the algal assimilation and ultimately contributed to increasing nutrient concentrations [ev_nutrient_removal_mcmi14_3]. In the fenced pasture buffer, the nutrient decline reversed after twelve years, once debris blockages became less common and aquatic macrophytes were shaded out by the now-established woody vegetation, and nutrient levels rose again — a long-term waning of the benefit, not a measured harm [ev_nutrient_removal_dosskey10_7]. The catchment-scale sediment and the general nitrogen-removal findings above are themselves citations within a review, not new measurement [ev_sediment_retention_dosskey10_6, ev_nutrient_removal_dosskey10_1, ev_nutrient_removal_dosskey10_2, ev_nutrient_removal_dosskey10_3, ev_nutrient_removal_dosskey10_7]. The thermal benefit can invert as well: newly restored streams whose canopy was removed during construction had higher temperatures [ev_stream_temperature_mcmi14_1], and that study is urban restoration bundled with channel regrading, where the reach-scale nitrate result rests on a sample of three and the phosphate comparison was not significant [ev_nutrient_removal_mcmi14_1, ev_nutrient_removal_mcmi14_2]. Context can remove the pathway entirely — buffers are not as effective where fields are tile drained, because the drains bypass them [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_6] — and cover type decides the outcome: a 20 m oat buffer had no significant effect on total phosphorus while a 10 m rye grass strip did [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_4, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_5], the grass strip did little to reduce phosphorus in shallow groundwater [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_3], and across the reviewed studies no clear pattern was evident for subsurface phosphorus, with one study finding concentrations increased [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_14]. Finally, the largest percentages in the pool are modelled, not measured: the Costa Rican nitrogen and phosphorus retention gains of 81.4 and 85.9% fall to 35.1 and 37.1% under the study's own low retention-efficiency assumption [ev_nutrient_removal_lang22_1, ev_nutrient_removal_lang22_2], and the Guishui paper reports both 58% and 92.8% for phosphorus in the same treatment [ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_4, ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_7]. The cooling evidence is from buffers left at harvest or from wooded strips in general; the only measurement on newly restored streams found that those with open canopy had higher temperatures [ev_stream_temperature_mcmi14_1], so cooling from a newly established strip is not shown here. Provenance is narrow: Illinois, Iowa, Kansas and Connecticut field sites — several of them repeat visits to the same Bear Creek reach — a pooled analysis that states no study country, and upper-middle-income work from China and Brazil; the Brazilian values are correlations whose authors stress that watershed-scale land cover explained water quality better than the riparian zone [ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_8]. No measurement here comes from a low-income farming system. The European figures are model results and the Quebec figures are cited second-hand; both come from rich countries [ev_nutrient_removal_englund21_4, ev_nutrient_removal_simard09_5, ev_stream_temperature_simard09_7].

Below rainfed row crops the strip removes what the runoff carries and what the shallow groundwater brings. effect_mechanism: Established or regrowing riparian vegetation removes load on three fronts. Dissolved nutrients are taken out as water passes through: shallow-groundwater nitrate fell by up to 90% behind the Illinois strips [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_1], with reviewed reductions of 79-98% in surface runoff, 68-100% and 40-100% in groundwater and subsurface waters for forested strips, and phosphorus reductions of 50-85% [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_10, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_7, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_8, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_12]; along the Guishui River an 18 m woody strip removed 89.8% of total nitrogen and retained 92.8% of total phosphorus, against 72.3% for grass and 43.9% for shrub cover and 17.62% with no buffer [ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_4, ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_5, ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_6, ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_7, ev_nutrient_removal_kumw24_8]; and the reviewed ranges for grass strips are markedly lower and more variable than for forested ones [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_8]; more broadly, riparian vegetation removes nitrogen through plant uptake and denitrification [ev_nutrient_removal_dosskey10_1], and in a long-term study of a trampled, overgrazed pasture riparian zone fenced off from livestock, rapid herbaceous and then woody regrowth was followed by declining stream nutrient levels over the first twelve years [ev_nutrient_removal_dosskey10_7]. Particles settle out: outflow sediment fell by 92%, 72% and 50% under woody, grass and shrub cover against a bare control trapping 22% [ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_1, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_2, ev_sediment_retention_kumw24_3], trapping efficiency rises sharply over the first 10 m of buffer [ev_sediment_retention_cole20_1], fairly narrow strips of riparian vegetation reduce sediment input to surface water [ev_sediment_retention_osbo93_15, ev_sediment_retention_schultz95_1, ev_sediment_retention_zhao13_1]; at catchment scale, restoring vegetation to denuded, livestock-trampled riparian zones reduced sediment export from over 100 to less than 10 kilograms per hectare per year within one year, mainly through less bank erosion and a stabilised channel [ev_sediment_retention_dosskey10_6], and in a Brazilian cotton field bordered by an existing native riparian forest, sediment eroded from the cropped slope formed layers up to 14 cm thick in trenches a few metres inside the forest, with no buried sediment layer found further in [ev_sediment_retention_oliv10_1]; and in Brazilian watersheds nitrogen, phosphorus, solids and faecal coliforms fall while dissolved oxygen rises as riparian forest cover increases [ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_3, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_4, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_5, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_6, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_7, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_8, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_9, ev_nutrient_removal_mello18_12, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_1, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_2, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_3, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_4, ev_nutrient_removal_zhao13_5, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_1, ev_sediment_retention_mello18_2]. Modelled at national scale, meeting Costa Rica's legal minimum raises nitrogen retention by 81.4% and phosphorus retention by 85.9%, with sediment retention up 3.9% [ev_nutrient_removal_lang22_1, ev_sediment_retention_lang22_1]. effect_mechanism: A planted strip works by settling, infiltration and uptake. Sediment-bound load is trapped: 70% and more than 92% of incoming sediment under simulated rainfall [ev_sediment_retention_lee00_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee00_2], 95% and 97% over natural events with a floor of 71% and 86% [ev_sediment_retention_lee03_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee03_3, ev_sediment_retention_lee03_7], 99.7% of suspended-solids mass in the Kansas plots [ev_sediment_retention_mank07_1], 97% behind an 8 m fescue strip and 91% within the first 4 m [ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_1, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_2, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_3, ev_sediment_retention_blanco04_4], and 92% of overland-flow suspended solids after a cropped strip was seeded to fescue [ev_sediment_retention_clau00_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_1, ev_sediment_retention_lee04_3, ev_sediment_retention_sira20_1]. Dissolved load is removed as water passes through: across 88 buffers, mean nitrogen removal effectiveness was 67.5%, at 0.394 mg per litre per metre [ev_nutrient_removal_maye07_1, ev_nutrient_removal_maye07_2]; the Bear Creek plantings removed 80% and 94% of total nitrogen over natural events and 64 to 93% under a 25 mm per hour simulation [ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_2, ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_4, ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_4, ev_nutrient_removal_lee00_5, ev_nutrient_removal_lee03_9, ev_nutrient_removal_schultz95_1]; a seeded Connecticut strip cut overland-flow total Kjeldahl nitrogen by 70%, nitrate by 83% and total phosphorus by 73% [ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_1, ev_nutrient_removal_clau00_5]; grass strips reduced nitrate in surface runoff by 54-84%, phosphorus by 61-83% and subsurface nitrogen by 10-60%, and 80 to 90% nitrate reduction was found in subsurface water after passage through grass and forest strips [ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_11, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_13, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_9, ev_nutrient_removal_osbo93_5, ev_nutrient_removal_schultz95_2, ev_nutrient_removal_blanco04_1, ev_nutrient_removal_blanco04_2, ev_nutrient_removal_blanco04_3, ev_nutrient_removal_mank07_1]; a separately reviewed US riparian zone that had been cleared and cropped for a long time and was then restored to grass cover (planting vs natural regrowth not stated) showed a 35% reduction in groundwater nitrate [ev_nutrient_removal_dosskey10_3]; and nutrients are locked into the planted biomass, 770 and 90 kg of nitrogen per hectare in the Quebec poplar buffers [ev_nutrient_removal_fort10_1]. Planted canopy also shades the water: wooded strips moderate diel temperature fluctuations, and buffers significantly reduced post-harvest temperature increases, with partially cut 10-20 m strips still shading the stream [ev_stream_temperature_cole20_1, ev_stream_temperature_lee04_1, ev_stream_temperature_lee04_2, ev_stream_temperature_lee04_3]. Newer sources point the same way. A European model of strips of willow, poplar or grass planted along watercourses finds they would avoid about 33% of all nitrogen reaching water in the EU and UK, and catch 19% of all soil lost by water erosion on cropland [ev_nutrient_removal_englund21_4, ev_sediment_retention_englund21_6]. A Quebec cost study, citing earlier Quebec research second-hand, reports nitrate falling by 47 to 100% and soluble phosphorus by 22 to 89% after wooded strips were planted, and states that without streamside vegetation stream water can be 2 to 10°C warmer [ev_nutrient_removal_simard09_5, ev_stream_temperature_simard09_7].
